title: Trace the work and grade the sources
learning_outcome: Specify trace fields and safe source tiers for the same workflow.
exercise: Draw one path from source to artifact to human review; classify each sample source.

boundaries.evidence: Use mock source IDs; keep private corpus and operational trace data outside the course.
boundaries.privacy: synthetic Harbor only; no actual participant, client, admin, or private corpus content
boundaries.authority: prepare_only; no live agent, memory promotion, message, booking, spending, or publication

scenes.narration_exact: “Morgan sees a line in the Harbor Session Option Brief: ‘The room can hold twenty people.’ Morgan asks where the number came from. A raw machine log might answer eventually, after someone searches through hundreds of entries. Morgan needs a shorter trail: the source that carried the number, the date it was checked, what the agent concluded, and the condition that would have stopped the draft. A trace should serve the person accountable for the work.”

scenes.narration_exact: “For our paper design, the trace has five questions. What did the agent prepare? What did it read? What would have stopped it? Where is the artifact? Who reviews it? Answer in plain language. ‘Prepared a draft comparison.’ ‘Read the room-capacity note.’ ‘Would hold if the note expired or conflicted with another source.’ ‘Saved the draft brief.’ ‘Morgan reviews.’ We can keep technical diagnostics elsewhere. The operator's view needs the load-bearing facts first.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Now inspect the source. A real document can still be old. A correct citation can still support a wrong current claim. Before the agent uses a source, record who created it, when it was observed, when it expires, what it may be used for, and where it may travel. In the Harbor case, the three course records help us practice a source contract. They are not evidence of actual attendance, room capacity, or staff availability.”

scenes.narration_exact: “The source ladder gives us four useful tiers: public safe, client safe, internal operations, and private. Public safe means cleared for the specific external use. Client safe stays inside that client's context. Internal operations can inform an internal draft but needs a reviewed rewrite before an external claim. Private material needs explicit access authority and stays out of this workshop exercise. A summary inherits the strictest tier of its sources. A missing tier means hold. A public link by itself does not prove that a document is current, accurate, or cleared for reuse.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Classify the three Harbor notes as classroom-only, with no publication permission. The capacity note has a course date and expires before the next planning cycle. The attendance note is an aggregate count, not a list of people. The facilitator note says only ‘available for review,’ not ‘confirmed to teach.’ That wording changes the recommendation. The brief may say ‘availability unconfirmed.’ It may not say the session is staffed. This is source safety doing practical work: it stops a small mismatch from becoming a confident plan.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Draw the path from source reference to draft to Morgan's review gate. Fill the five trace answers for one course run. Then classify each source: tier, owner, observed date, expiry, read use, quote use, memory use, and publish use. If a source has no attribution or is too old for the decision, mark the brief blocked. Use a fictional or approved example. Do not use private operational data. We are designing the gate, not operating it.”
